To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

deans and heads of accounting departments at AACSB-acccredited institutions rate the relative importance of scholarly accomplishments in promotion decisions of accounting faculty in the following descending order: (1) publication, (2) recognition, (3) funding, (4) teaching, (5) service, and (6) technology.
deans and accounting department chairs place the highest importance on scholarly activities involving academic publications and external recognition in their promotion and tenure decisions.

deans and accounting department chairs rate academic publications and awards as the highest importance for tenure and promotion of accounting faculty, and the importance assigned to various academic accomplishments varies by institutional type.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how accounting faculty members should spend their scholarly time in light of the importance assigned to various types of scholarly activity by deans and heads of accounting departments.
the importance that deans and accounting department chairs place on various scholarly accomplishments in tenure and promotion.
the importance of various scholarly accomplishments in tenure and promotion of accounting faculty.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

deans and accounting department leaders at AACSB-acccredited institutions consider a broad range of scholarly activities in their tenure and promotion decisions, but that certain scholarly accomplishments, particularly academic publication activities and awards, are more important than other accomplishments.

the scholarly accomplishments that count most in tenure decisions of accounting faculties at AACSB-acredited institutions are those that are most visible to the accounting community and that are most likely to be recognized and rewarded by the accounting community.
the importance assigned to scholarly accomplishments varies by institutional type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the importance of scholarly accomplishments in tenure and promotion is not uniform across all types of institutions.

the scholarly accomplishments that matter most to deans and accounting department chairs in promotion and tenure decision-making are the same ones that matter most to accounting faculty members in their pursuit of scholarly activities.
the definition of scholarly accomplishment in the promotion and tenure decision process is not uniform across institutions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
accounting faculty members should be cognizant of the importance that their deans and department heads place on various scholarly accomplishments.
the scholarly activities and accomplishments valued in accounting departments vary with the educational missions and institutional types of the colleges of business in which these departments reside.
accounting faculty should consider their institution's classification when determining which scholarly accomplishments will be most important in their promotion and tenure cases.
